stem: A car starts from rest and accelerates uniformly to 27 m/s in 9 s. How far does it travel in that time?
eli5: When speed builds up steadily from zero, the average speed is half the final speed. Distance is that average speed times the time.
solution:
Acceleration a = \frac{27}{9} = 3 m/s^{2}.

Distance s = \frac{1}{2}at^{2} = \frac{1}{2}(3)(9)^{2} = 121.5 m.

Check: average speed 13.5 m/s × 9 s = 121.5 m.

stem: A 50 kg crate is pulled along a level floor by a 300 N horizontal force. The coefficient of kinetic friction is 0.30. What is the acceleration of the crate? Use g = 9.81 m/s^{2}.
eli5: Friction eats part of the pull. Whatever push is left over is what actually speeds the crate up.

stem: A 2 kg ball is dropped from rest from a height of 10 m. Ignoring air resistance, how fast is it moving just before it lands? Use g = 9.81 m/s^{2}.
eli5: Height is stored energy. As the ball falls, all of that stored energy turns into speed. The mass cancels out, so a heavy ball and a light ball land at the same speed.

stem: A thin uniform rod has a mass of 6 kg and a length of 2 m. What is its mass moment of inertia about an axis through one end, perpendicular to the rod?
eli5: A rod is harder to swing from its end than to spin about its middle, because more of its mass is far from the pivot.
solution:
About one end: I = \frac{mL^{2}}{3} = \frac{6(2)^{2}}{3} = 8 kg·m^{2}.

About the centre it would be \frac{mL^{2}}{12} = 2 kg·m^{2}.

stem: A ball is launched from level ground at 20 m/s, at 30° above the horizontal. Ignoring air resistance, how far away does it land? Use g = 9.81 m/s^{2}.
eli5: The ball moves sideways at a steady speed while gravity pulls it back down. How long it stays in the air decides how far it gets.

stem: A car travels at a constant 20 m/s around a curve of radius 80 m. What is its acceleration toward the centre of the curve?
eli5: Even at steady speed, turning means the direction of travel keeps changing. That change is an acceleration pointing into the turn.

stem: A solid uniform disk has a mass of 10 kg and a radius of 0.3 m. What is its mass moment of inertia about its central axis?
eli5: A disk is easier to spin than a ring of the same mass, because much of its mass sits near the middle.

stem: A block slides down a frictionless incline at 30° to the horizontal. What is its acceleration? Use g = 9.81 m/s^{2}.
eli5: Only the part of gravity that points down the slope speeds the block up. The rest presses it into the surface.
solution:
a = g sin 30° = 9.81(0.5) = 4.91 m/s^{2}.

The mass cancels.

stem: A net torque of 12 N·m acts on a flywheel with a mass moment of inertia of 3 kg·m^{2}. What is its angular acceleration?
eli5: Torque is the turning version of force, and moment of inertia is the turning version of mass.

stem: A hoist lifts a 500 kg load at a constant 2 m/s. What power is delivered to the load? Use g = 9.81 m/s^{2}.
eli5: Power is how fast work is done. Lifting a heavier load, or lifting faster, takes more power.

stem: A spring with a stiffness of 2,000 N/m is compressed 0.1 m and released against a 0.5 kg block on a frictionless surface. What speed does the block reach?
eli5: A squeezed spring stores energy. When it lets go, that energy becomes the block's motion.
